questions.q: In a STAR answer, where should most of your time go?
options: Situation, since context matters most
Result only
Action, meaning what you personally did
The interviewer's background
questions.explain: Roughly 60% of the story should be your own actions; situation and task should be brief.

questions.q: Which is the best source of behavioral stories for a career changer?
options: Invented achievements that sound impressive
Real decisions from your projects, such as catching leakage or choosing a metric
Job duties copied from a posting
Stories about other people's work
questions.explain: Real project decisions are truthful, specific and demonstrate judgment; invented stories collapse under follow-up questions.

questions.q: Why is saying 'we' throughout a story a problem?
options: It sounds too humble to be believed
It shows poor grammar
It is against interview rules
The interviewer cannot tell what you personally did
questions.explain: Interviewers evaluate your contribution, so be clear about your actions while crediting others honestly.

questions.q: Which is the better way to explain a churn model to a business stakeholder?
options: It scores each customer on cancel risk; contacting the top group reaches more leavers than random, and we should test the outreach
It uses gradient boosting optimized for AUC
It is a black box, so trust it
It has 100% accuracy
questions.explain: Focus on the decision, compare to a simple alternative, and state limits and a next step, without jargon.

questions.q: How should you answer 'Tell me about a mistake you made'?
options: Say you have never made one
Blame a teammate
Describe a real, modest mistake, own it, and explain what you changed afterward
Give a strength disguised as a weakness
questions.explain: Interviewers look for honesty and learning; a specific mistake with a concrete change shows both.
